main_text.p: si enim veteres hastis, id est con-tis, inter se depugnét, uti hodie solent concurrere gladiatores? Id certè minore eveniet cum periculo, quàm si veloci equo-rum cursu lanceis acuminatis, vel aliter concurrant. Atque adeo non valeret argumentum à ludis veterum desumptum, & quidem minùs periculosis , ad eos ludos, qui maximo cum periculo sunt conjuncti. Verùm evidentiorem responsionem suppeditat ipsa lex. Non dicitur licere hastis aut pilis in se mutuò irruere, verùm conceditur hastâ, aut pilo jaciendo, virtutis causâ certare. Ut nullum hisce in ludis parti ab adversâ parte fit periculum. Tantùm enim vires exploran-tur, uter certantium hastâ aut pilum longiùs emittere, vel, e-vibrare valeat. Non aliter atq; inter milites recepta confue-tudo, ut artuum robur explo-rent,

page.notes: The page has an ornament mark in the right margin and small specks at the bottom left, which are not printed text. Many words are set with long-s forms (for example "fi", "haftis", "folent", "curfu"), which I have transcribed with plain s. "rent," is the completion of the hyphenated word "explo-rent," and is part of the text, not a catchword. Printed spacing before the comma in "periculosis ," is kept as printed.
